title: HunterHR
tagline: AI-powered HR automation platform for screening, scheduling, and candidate communication.

overview.text:
HunterHR is an AI-powered, end-to-end recruitment automation platform designed to streamline hiring workflows across email, WhatsApp, resume parsing, candidate scoring, and interview scheduling.

Recruiters can create job openings with weighted criteria, automatically ingest applicant resumes via Gmail and WhatsApp scans, rank candidates using Ollama (LLaMA 3) and Qdrant vector embeddings, schedule interview slots synced with Google Calendar, and dispatch personalized offer or rejection letters using a rich-text template editor.

Originally prototyped with React, the system was completely re-architected into a modern Nuxt 4 full-stack platform with a high-throughput backend, responsive Nuxt UI v4 interface, and local AI inference.

userManual: User Story 1: Defining a Job Opening & AI Evaluation Criteria As a recruiter launching a new hiring drive: 1. Navigate to the Jobs page and create a new position with job title, salary band, qualifications, and locations. 2. Configure custom evaluation weights (technical skills, work experience, projects) and define the minimum passing score threshold. 3. Choose automated or manual shortlisting mode, then publish the job requisition. User Story 2: Automated Multi-Channel Resume Sourcing As an HR team collecting candidate applications: 1. Open the Scanners dashboard to activate candidate sourcing pipelines. 2. Connect your recruitment Gmail account to automatically scan and ingest PDF resumes from incoming emails. 3. Link designated WhatsApp hiring groups using a quick QR code scan to capture resumes shared in group chats. 4. Let the platform automatically extract text, remove duplicate submissions, and catalog candidate resumes. User Story 3: AI Candidate Shortlisting & Profile Review As a hiring manager reviewing applicant fit: 1. Visit the Candidates table to inspect all processed applicants ranked by AI match scores. 2. Filter applicants by score range, required skills, experience level, or status (Shortlisted, Selected, Rejected). 3. Open any candidate record to review suitability breakdown, key qualifications, and the original resume file. 4. Update candidate status with a single click to progress them through the recruitment pipeline. User Story 4: Interview Scheduling & Calendar Sync As an interview coordinator organizing evaluation rounds: 1. Navigate to the Interviews page and create interview sessions with defined time slots, meeting mode (online video link or office location), and attendee capacity. 2. Sync the schedule directly with Google Calendar to maintain real-time calendar availability without double-booking. 3. Click Smart Auto-Assign to automatically distribute top-ranked shortlisted candidates into available interview slots, or assign slots manually. User Story 5: Automated Candidate Communication & Template Dispatch As an HR specialist communicating outcomes: 1. Open the Email Templates editor to design personalized message templates for interview invites, offer letters, or polite rejections. 2. Insert dynamic variables (such as candidate name, interview time, role title, and compensation offer) for automated personalization. 3. Dispatch emails individually or in bulk directly from the portal to keep candidates informed at every stage.

items.caption: Jobs Page — Job Description Management & AI Scoring Weights
Scanners Page — WhatsApp Connection & Gmail Resume Scanner
Candidates Table — AI-Scored & Filterable Shortlisted Applicants
Interviews Page — Event Scheduler, Google Calendar Sync & Slot Assignment
Email Templates — Drag-and-Drop & Rich Text Template Editor

devNotes: Tech Stack Nuxt 4, Vue 3, Nuxt UI v4, TailwindCSS v4, TypeScript, Node.js (Nitro / H3), PostgreSQL 15, Qdrant Vector DB, Redis, Ollama (LLaMA 3 / Phi-3), Docker, Google Workspace APIs (Gmail & Calendar), WhatsApp-web.js (Puppeteer), Tiptap Editor, ImageKit Evolution & Migration Originally developed and prototyped as a React + Node.js client-server application, HunterHR was fully redesigned and re-engineered into an all-in-one full-stack Nuxt 4 (Vue 3) application. The rewrite leveraged Nuxt server routes (Nitro/H3), reactive Nuxt UI components, and TailwindCSS v4 for unified developer ergonomics, faster SSR rendering, and robust state management. AI Pipeline & Vector Search Resumes parsed from PDF streams are embedded using BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 into Qdrant for semantic cosine-similarity matching against active job requirements. Ollama runs local LLaMA 3 / Phi-3 models to classify application emails and validate candidate suitability with zero external data leakage. Automation & Integration Features background ingestion pipelines via WhatsApp-web.js (headless Puppeteer) and Gmail API, Google Calendar synchronization for two-way interview scheduling, and ImageKit CDN for persistent asset storage.

title: OldMonkey

overview.text: My journey of touch typing started back in high school. I spent months on keybr.com to unlearn bad habits and learn touch typing from scratch, then migrated to monkeytype.com to push my raw speed. Naturally, I wanted to build a tribute to the community that made me faster. OldMonkey is a real-time multiplayer typing game where players compete head-to-head, chasing live opponent cursors through paragraphs while WPM and accuracy update every keystroke.

userManual: User Story 1: Joining the Arena & Account Setup As a player entering the competitive typing arena: 1. Sign up using email OTP verification or sign in instantly with Google. 2. Access your profile dashboard displaying your starting competitive rating of 500. User Story 2: Solo Practice Against the Adaptive Bot As a typist warming up and pushing raw speed limits: 1. Launch Bot Mode to enter a single-player challenge against the adaptive bot engine. 2. Race against the bot as it dynamically benchmarks ~8 WPM above your personal best to push your speed limits. 3. Track real-time typing speed (WPM) and accuracy metrics updating live with every keystroke. User Story 3: Live Multiplayer Matchmaking & Head-to-Head Racing As a competitive typist challenging rivals: 1. Search for online players by username or filter opponents within specific WPM brackets (e.g., 60–70 WPM) for balanced races. 2. Send direct match invites or join public race lobbies. 3. Race head-to-head while watching your opponent's ghost cursor move character-by-character across the paragraph in real time. 4. Win races to climb the competitive ladder with transparent +5 / -5 rating adjustments. User Story 4: Social Interaction & Progress Tracking As an active player monitoring personal growth: 1. Use in-game chat to message rivals, celebrate victories, and coordinate rematch challenges. 2. Review your game history to inspect past WPM charts, accuracy trends, and long-term typing milestones.

items.caption: User profile, game history, room creation, find players

devNotes: Architecture Event-driven real-time system using WebSockets for character-by-character synchronization and long polling for chats. Stack Python, FastAPI, WebSockets, Redis, MongoDB, JWT, Google OIDC, Argon2 Real-Time Sync Redis manages all live game state and timer synchronization, keeping latency sub-second across concurrent matches. Ghost Cursors stream opponent position updates to all connected clients via WebSocket. Monkey Engine A custom adaptive bot built in Python that reads the player's top speed and targets roughly 8 WPM higher — scaling dynamically so the challenge never plateaus. Auth Full authentication pipeline with JWT sessions, Google OIDC login, OTP email verification, and Argon2 password hashing.

title: Testron
tagline: An evaluation platform with real-time testing, coding evaluation, and classroom management.

overview.text: An end-to-end online examination platform designed for coaching institutes, teachers, and students to conduct secure and scalable assessments. The platform supports MCQ, numerical, and coding-based examinations with advanced evaluation logic inspired by competitive exams like JEE and NTA-based assessments. The system includes separate teacher and student portals, classroom management, scheduled and deadline-based tests, automatic evaluation, topic-wise analytics, and isolated Docker sandboxes for executing programming questions securely.

userManual: User Story 1: Classroom Setup & Student Onboarding (Teacher) As an educator managing a student cohort: 1. Create and manage virtual classrooms or study batches from the Teacher portal. 2. Share unique classroom invite codes or invitation links with students. 3. Review and approve or reject student join requests directly from the dashboard. User Story 2: Comprehensive Assessment Authoring (Teacher) As an instructor designing an examination: 1. Create a new test with custom scheduling (live real-time window or deadline-based attempt window) and time limits. 2. Configure flexible marking schemes: assign full marks for correct answers, negative marking for wrong attempts, and partial marking for multi-select questions. 3. Add diverse problem types including MCQs, numerical inputs, and programming challenges with test cases. 4. Upload question images, reference assets, and formatted code snippets. User Story 3: Real-Time Examination Experience (Student) As a student taking a live test: 1. Join the classroom using the group code and launch the active exam. 2. Navigate between questions using the question palette, flag questions for review, and track the live countdown timer. 3. Write solutions for coding problems in the integrated editor with instant execution feedback against test cases. 4. Stay focused within the exam tab: switching browser tabs triggers automated proctoring alerts and auto-submits upon repeated violations. User Story 4: Instant Result Evaluation & Performance Analytics (Teacher & Student) As a student and educator reviewing assessment outcomes: 1. Receive instant automated score computation immediately after submitting the exam. 2. Students can view detailed answer keys, solution explanations, and execution results for coding test cases. 3. Teachers can inspect class-wide submission summaries, score distributions, and topic-wise analytics to identify areas for student improvement.
devNotes: Architecture The platform follows a modular Django app-based architecture separating authentication, classroom management, testing, evaluation, analytics, and sandbox execution into independent domains. Backend Stack - Django - PostgreSQL - Redis - Docker - Docker Compose Authentication Implemented email OTP authentication using Redis for temporary OTP storage along with Google OIDC login using OAuth 2.0. Realtime & Timer Logic Redis was used for managing volatile exam state such as countdown timers, OTP expiry, and rapid-fire question timing. Code Execution Sandbox Coding questions are executed inside isolated Docker containers to securely run untrusted user code with controlled resources and hidden test cases. Evaluation Engine Built a custom scoring engine supporting: - Negative marking - Partial marking for MCQs - Numerical answer validation - Hidden test case evaluation - Auto-generated result computation.

title: 925buddy
tagline: An AI-driven job search engine that automates job discovery, matching, and monitoring.

overview.text:
As a fresher actively applying for jobs myself, I wanted to build something that solves the “tab-fatigue” most job-seekers face.

Job hunting today feels like a full-time unpaid job in itself.
Two hours on LinkedIn and Indeed… and Wellfound still left.
Eyes burning. Tabs everywhere.

Most of us spend hours reading roles we don’t even qualify for: scrolling past Laravel jobs when our stack is Django, manually tracking what we applied to, and repeating the same searches every single day.

So I built 925buddy: a backend-first, AI-driven job search engine that scrapes, understands, matches, and monitors jobs automatically, so users stop searching and start receiving.

userManual: User Story 1: Resume Upload & Profile Intelligence As a job seeker starting your search: 1. Upload your resume in PDF format to the platform. 2. The system automatically analyzes your technical skills, work history, and target roles to construct your job-seeking profile. User Story 2: Multi-Portal Job Aggregation & Centralized Discovery As an applicant eliminating tab fatigue: 1. Trigger automated job scraping across major portals (Indeed, Naukri) from a single interface. 2. View all aggregated listings in a unified dashboard equipped with pagination, role filters, and location tags. 3. Review clean, deduplicated job postings with highlighted key requirements matching your background. User Story 3: Conversational AI Career Assistant As a candidate seeking personalized guidance: 1. Open the interactive career chatbot to ask questions about scraped jobs and your resume. 2. Inquire with prompts like: “Which jobs fit my profile best?”, “What skills am I missing for senior backend roles?”, or “Draft a tailored application note for this role.” 3. Receive accurate, hallucination-free advice directly matching your skills against active job descriptions. User Story 4: Background Monitoring & Instant Match Alerts As a busy professional monitoring opportunities passively: 1. Schedule daily or weekly background scraping routines. 2. Let the automated agent continuously scout portals for new openings matching your criteria. 3. Receive email notifications whenever high-match opportunities are discovered so you can apply early.

items.caption: Get jobs from multiple portals like Naukri, Indeed etc. in a centralized dashbaord.
Talk with the chatbot to get perfect jobs that match your skills, to get hot skills in the market or anything you want to know related to jobs and your skills.

devNotes: From the developer's perspective This system is built as a RAG + async backend pipeline: 🔹 Data ingestion ◽ Selenium + BeautifulSoup scrape full job descriptions ◽ Jobs are normalized and stored in MongoDB ◽ Each job is tagged to a specific user (multi-tenant design) 🔹 Resume intelligence ◽ PDF resumes are uploaded and stored securely in ImageKit ◽ Text extracted via PyMuPDF ◽ Chunked using LangChain RecursiveTextSplitter ◽ Embedded with Sentence Transformers 🔹 Vector search & RAG ◽ Job + resume embeddings stored in ChromaDB ◽ On every query: - Relevant resume + job chunks retrieved via cosine similarity - Context passed to Groq LLM - Strict RAG guardrails prevent hallucination if no data exists 🔹 Proactive search agent ◽ Celery + Redis (RedBeat) handle scheduled scraping ◽ Background workers: - Scrape jobs - Embed new data - Compute similarity scores - Trigger email alerts if score exceeds threshold 🔹 Backend & infra ◽ FastAPI (JWT auth, protected routes) ◽ MongoDB (users, jobs, metadata) ◽ ChromaDB (vector store) ◽ Docker + Docker Compose (Redis, workers) ◽ Fully async, non-blocking architecture Tech Stack FastAPI, Python, MongoDB, ChromaDB, Celery, Redis, Docker, Groq LLM, Sentence Transformers, Selenium, BeautifulSoup, PyMuPDF, LangChain, ImageKit

title: Jimi
tagline: A full-featured musical instrument marketplace and social platform for musicians and guitar enthusiasts.

overview.text: Jimi is a modern guitar and musical instrument marketplace platform that combines e-commerce, community interaction, and admin-driven business management into a single ecosystem. The platform allows users to browse and purchase musical instruments, check delivery availability using pin codes and shop radius validation, track orders, and interact with a moderated social feed built for musicians. Admins can manage inventory, products, orders, discounts, and community moderation through a dedicated dashboard, while users get a seamless shopping and community experience tailored for music enthusiasts.

userManual: User Story 1: Instrument Browsing & Seamless Ordering (Shopper / Musician) As a musician looking for new instruments and gear: 1. Browse electric and acoustic guitars, amplifiers, and musical accessories with intuitive category and price filters. 2. Enter your postal pin code on product pages to verify local delivery availability and estimated arrival times. 3. Add items to your shopping cart and complete purchase through a secure online payment checkout. 4. Track order progress and shipping status from your account dashboard. User Story 2: Musician Community & Social Feed (Musician) As a guitar enthusiast connecting with fellow players: 1. Explore a dedicated social feed featuring gear demos, playing clips, and musician discussions. 2. Create and publish posts to showcase your instruments, share technique tips, or ask for gear recommendations. 3. Like, comment on, and save community posts to your personal collection. User Story 3: Store Inventory & Community Moderation (Admin) As a store owner managing business operations: 1. Add and manage instrument listings with product specs, photos, pricing, and stock levels. 2. Manage customer orders, track fulfillment states, and configure promotional discount codes. 3. Moderate community discussions and posts through admin moderation tools to ensure a healthy community environment.
devNotes: Built With FastAPI, Python, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, SQLAlchemy, Docker, Docker Compose, NGINX, Celery, Razorpay, ImageKit Architecture The platform was designed as a modular backend system combining e-commerce, order management, payments, inventory handling, and a social media layer for musicians. PostgreSQL was used for transactional systems like users and orders, while MongoDB handled product catalogs and social content. Redis and Celery powered background workflows such as notifications, asynchronous processing, and session handling. The application was containerized using Docker and structured for scalable deployment and service orchestration.

title: Bluff Game
tagline: A real-time multiplayer bluff card game with live chat and peer-to-peer video communication.

overview.text: Bluff Game is a real-time multiplayer implementation of the classic Bluff (Cheat) card game designed for interactive online gameplay. The platform allows players to create and join game rooms, play live matches with synchronized turns and card actions, communicate through in-room chat, and connect using built-in video and voice calling. The experience combines competitive gameplay with social interaction, creating a lightweight virtual game room where players can bluff, challenge, react, and communicate in real time.

userManual: User Story 1: Game Room Creation & Inviting Friends As a host organizing a virtual card game night: 1. Log in and create a new multiplayer game room with a custom room code. 2. Share the room link or code with 2 to 4 friends to assemble players in the lobby. 3. Launch the live match once all participants have entered the room. User Story 2: Playing the Live Bluff Card Match As a player making moves and challenging opponents: 1. Receive your dealt hand and wait for your turn indicator. 2. Select cards from your hand and submit your claim (e.g., “Three Kings”) face-down into the center pile. 3. Challenge the previous player by calling “Bluff!” if you suspect their claim does not match the cards played. 4. Watch the automated card reveal animation: if the claim was a bluff, the bluffer collects the pile; if truthful, the challenger takes the cards. 5. Discard all cards from your hand first to claim victory. User Story 3: Real-Time Audio, Video & In-Game Chat As players interacting socially at the table: 1. Turn on your camera and microphone for built-in peer-to-peer video and voice communication. 2. Read opponents’ expressions and verbal cues in real time to catch bluffs. 3. Use the integrated text chat to send quick messages and game banter during play.

items.caption: Real-time bluff gameplay and card actions

devNotes: Built With FastAPI, Python, WebSockets, WebRTC, MongoDB, JWT Authentication, Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3 Architecture The platform uses WebSockets for synchronized multiplayer gameplay and room-based real-time communication. WebRTC was integrated for peer-to-peer video and voice calling, while MongoDB handled room state and user data persistence. The application was designed as a multi-page real-time system with asynchronous backend handling for concurrent player actions and low-latency interaction.

title: Gmail Organizer
tagline: An AI-powered Gmail automation system for inbox organization, classification, and smart email workflows.

overview.text:
Gmail Organizer is an AI-driven inbox management platform designed to automate how users handle and organize their emails.

The system connects directly to Gmail accounts and uses intelligent agent workflows to scan inboxes, classify emails, generate summaries, draft responses, and perform automated cleanup actions such as archiving or deleting low-value messages.

Built with a modular agent architecture, the platform focuses on reducing inbox overload while providing users with a cleaner, more organized email experience.

userManual: User Story 1: Secure Account Connection & Inbox Ingestion As a user overwhelmed by unorganized emails: 1. Connect your Gmail account securely using Google OAuth authentication. 2. Initiate an automated scan to ingest recent threads, unread emails, and subscriptions. User Story 2: Intelligent Classification & Daily Digest As a professional managing incoming communication: 1. View emails automatically sorted into structured categories: Urgent/Action Required, OTPs & Transactions, Newsletters, and Promotions. 2. Read an AI-generated daily inbox summary that highlights critical deadlines, key questions, and pending follow-ups. User Story 3: AI Reply Drafting & Fast Follow-Ups As a user responding to important messages: 1. Select an email requiring action and click “Draft Reply”. 2. Review contextually generated draft replies tailored to the sender’s tone and inquiry. 3. Edit, refine, and send replies directly from the dashboard or save to Gmail drafts. User Story 4: Automated Inbox Cleanup & Archival As a user striving for Inbox Zero: 1. Apply automated cleanup routines to archive expired OTPs, notifications, and promotional emails. 2. Bulk-archive or delete unwanted messages with one click while safeguarding critical business correspondence.
devNotes: Built With FastAPI, Python, CrewAI, Google OAuth 2.0, Gmail API Architecture The system was designed using an agent-based workflow architecture separating email analysis and execution into independent components. CrewAI was used for orchestrating the automation pipeline, while Gmail API integration enabled inbox access, classification, and automated actions. The backend was built as an async-friendly modular API system with extensibility for future real-time streaming and background task processing.

title: Tubedown
tagline: A lightweight media downloader for YouTube videos, playlists, audio, and subtitles.

overview.text: A simple cross-platform downloader designed to make saving YouTube content fast and accessible. The application allows users to download single videos, entire playlists, audio as MP3, and subtitles in SRT format through a clean and minimal interface. I initially built the project as a lightweight backend utility using Python and FastAPI to experiment with media streaming and download automation. Later, the project was migrated to a Flutter mobile application to provide a smoother mobile experience and better usability.

userManual: User Story 1: Downloading Single Videos & Audio As a user saving media for offline viewing: 1. Paste any YouTube video or short link into the download input bar. 2. Choose your preferred download format: full video (MP4) in available quality options or audio-only extraction (MP3). 3. Start the download and save the file directly to your local device. User Story 2: Batch Downloading Complete Playlists As a student or creator archiving educational or music series: 1. Paste a playlist link into the input field. 2. Select whether to download the entire playlist as individual video files or convert all tracks to MP3 audio files. 3. Download the complete series in an organized batch archive. User Story 3: Extracting Subtitles & Transcripts As a researcher or language learner needing textual content: 1. Paste the video link and select the Subtitle extraction option. 2. Select your desired language from the available subtitle tracks. 3. Download the formatted SRT subtitle file ready for study or media players.
devNotes: Built With - Python - FastAPI - pytubefix - ffmpeg - Flutter - Dart Backend Functionality The backend handled video streaming, playlist processing, MP3 extraction, subtitle generation, and ZIP-based batch downloads using the pytubefix library. Mobile Application The project was later migrated to Flutter by my friend Ratnadeep to provide a faster and more polished mobile experience with improved download handling and file management.

title: OLX CGEC
tagline: A college marketplace platform for buying, selling, and managing student listings securely.

overview.text:
OLX CGEC is a college-focused marketplace platform built to simplify buying and selling within the campus community.

The platform allows students to create listings, upload product images, manage their posts, and securely process payments through an integrated checkout flow.

userManual: User Story 1: Campus Registration & Student Account As a college student joining the campus trading platform: 1. Register for an account and log in to access verified campus listings. 2. Set up your user profile with contact details and campus hostel/day-scholar information. User Story 2: Listing Items for Sale As a student selling textbooks, electronics, cycles, or hostel essentials: 1. Click “Sell Item” to create a new marketplace post. 2. Fill in the title, category, description, and pricing for your listing. 3. Upload clear photos of the item and publish it to the student marketplace. 4. Edit, update, or remove your listings from your personal dashboard at any time. User Story 3: Browsing & Purchasing from Campus Peers As a buyer looking for affordable campus items: 1. Browse marketplace listings using category filters and search keywords. 2. View detailed product pages to inspect photos, condition, and seller details. 3. Proceed to checkout and pay securely using the integrated Razorpay payment gateway. 4. Receive payment verification and arrange on-campus handover with the seller.

items.caption: My items on sale, you can edit/delete

devNotes: Built With FastAPI, Python, PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, JWT Authentication, ImageKit, Razorpay, Docker, Docker Compose, Uvicorn Architecture The application uses a FastAPI backend with JWT-based authentication and PostgreSQL for persistent data storage. Image uploads are handled through ImageKit, while Razorpay was integrated for secure payment processing and order verification. Docker and Docker Compose were used to containerize the backend and database for simplified deployment and local development.
